picoquic/bbr.c:BBRCheckPathSaturated.analysis: Confirmed Phase 4D mismatch: Rust had the saturation predicate translated but skipped the enabled RTTJitterBufferProbe caller path in ProbeBW DOWN and CRUISE.
picoquic/bbr.c:BBRCheckPathSaturated.confirmation_analysis: Rust predicate and state updates match the C function, and the repaired ProbeBW DOWN/CRUISE caller ordering now matches the enabled C RTTJitterBufferProbe paths with early returns on saturation.
picoquic/bbr.c:BBRCheckPathSaturated.fix_summary: Called check_path_saturated from ProbeBwDown after check_time_to_probe_bw and from ProbeBwCruise before check_time_to_probe_bw, returning immediately on saturation to match C.

picoquic/bbr.c:BBRResetCongestionSignals.analysis: Confirmed Rust omitted the RTTJitterBuffer congestion signal reset present in C.
picoquic/bbr.c:BBRResetCongestionSignals.confirmation_analysis: Rust reset_congestion_signals now matches C by clearing loss_in_round, rtt_too_high_in_round, bw_latest, and inflight_latest; reset_lower_bounds remains a separate adjacent helper as in C.

picoquic/bbr.c:BBRStartProbeBW_DOWN.analysis: Confirmed C `BBRExpTest(..., do_rapid_start)` expands to true in this build, so the early probe wait must not depend on `exp_flags.do_rapid_start`.
picoquic/bbr.c:BBRStartProbeBW_DOWN.confirmation_analysis: C `BBRExpTest(..., do_rapid_start)` expands to true because the macro is selected before the local `BBRExperiment` define, and current Rust now gates the early wait only on `probe_probe_bw_quickly` while preserving the remaining state updates.
picoquic/bbr.c:BBRStartProbeBW_DOWN.fix_summary: Removed the `exp_flags.do_rapid_start` gate from `start_probe_bw_down`; early probe wait now depends only on `probe_probe_bw_quickly`.

picoquic/bbr.c:BBRUpdateProbeBWCyclePhas.analysis: Current Rust already has the active RTTJitterBufferProbe saturation early returns in the C order for ProbeBwDown and ProbeBwCruise.
picoquic/bbr.c:BBRUpdateProbeBWCyclePhas.confirmation_analysis: Current Rust now matches the active C RTTJitterBufferProbe path: ProbeBwDown calls check_time_to_probe_bw before check_path_saturated, ProbeBwCruise calls check_path_saturated before check_time_to_probe_bw, and both saturation hits return early after the helper enters Drain. The helper body mirrors BBRCheckPathSaturated and RTTJitterBufferProbe is defined in C.

picoquic/bbr1.c:picoquic_bbr1_notify.analysis: Confirmed mismatch: Rust used the notified path pacing packet time, while C uses cnx->path[0] for the long-RTT HyStart test.
picoquic/bbr1.c:picoquic_bbr1_notify.confirmation_analysis: Rust now uses the connection first path pacing packet time for the long-RTT HyStart test, matching C's cnx->path[0] source; the path_x fallback only covers an absent first path in Rust.
picoquic/bbr1.c:picoquic_bbr1_notify.fix_summary: Changed BBR1 notify to use cnx.paths.first().pacing.packet_time_microsec, falling back to path_x pacing when no first path exists.

picoquic/c4.c:c4_era_check.analysis: Confirmed mismatch: Rust era_check used the path-only lowest_not_ack helper, which cannot select the connection application packet context when multipath is disabled.
picoquic/c4.c:c4_era_check.confirmation_analysis: Rust now matches the C ready-state gate and lowest_not_ack context selection: path packet context under multipath, connection Application context otherwise, then compares against era_sequence.
picoquic/c4.c:c4_era_check.fix_summary: Added a c4-local lowest_not_ack selector matching picoquic_cc_get_lowest_not_ack: path packet context for multipath, connection Application packet context otherwise; era_check now uses it.

picoquic/c4.c:c4_init.analysis: C4 is now wired through a real congestion-control init path matching C allocation/reuse, option propagation, reset, and lost-feedback subscription behavior.
picoquic/c4.c:c4_init.confirmation_analysis: Rust now allocates or reuses C4State, sets connection.is_lost_feedback_notification_required, resets with the supplied option string, stores the state back on path.congestion_alg_state, and the c4 registry entry dispatches through C4_CONTROL with owning-connection access.
picoquic/c4.c:c4_init.fix_summary: Added c4_init and C4CongestionControl, wired the c4 registry entry to it, extended alg_init to receive the owning connection, preserved default/init option strings, and stored/reused C4State in path.congestion_alg_state.

picoquic/cc_common.c:picoquic_cc_get_low.analysis: The Rust path-only method could not match C single-path behavior because C selects through path_x->cnx. The method now uses the provided Connection to choose the same packet context as C.
picoquic/cc_common.c:picoquic_cc_get_low.confirmation_analysis: Current Rust selects the same packet context as C for multipath vs single-path, returns the lowest pending sequence when present, and otherwise uses wrapping highest_acknowledged + 1.
picoquic/cc_common.c:picoquic_cc_get_low.fix_summary: Changed PathCc::lowest_not_ack to accept &Connection, select path.pkt_ctx only for multipath and connection.pkt_ctx[Application] for single-path, and use wrapping_add(1) for C unsigned increment behavior.

picoquic/cc_common.c:picoquic_cc_increas.analysis: Confirmed mismatch repaired: Rust now computes the window increase from previous_window and primary-path rtt_min using the Reno threshold and satellite RTT cap, matching the C formula.
picoquic/cc_common.c:picoquic_cc_increas.confirmation_analysis: Rust now uses the primary path rtt_min and matches the C Reno-threshold/satellite-cap scaling formula; Duration ticks are microseconds matching the C constants. Saturating overflow and empty-path fallback are acceptable safe-pathology differences under the translation rules.
picoquic/cc_common.c:picoquic_cc_increas.fix_summary: Replaced the path cwin placeholder with the translated C formula in Connection::cc_increased_window.

picoquic/cc_common.c:picoquic_cc_slow_st.analysis: Phase 4D was correct: the Rust helper used path-local bytes_in_transit/cwin instead of the connection-level cwin_blocked latch used by C.
picoquic/cc_common.c:picoquic_cc_slow_st.confirmation_analysis: Rust now gates slow-start growth on connection.cwin_blocked, and the helper variants plus BBR, BBR1, Cubic, and Prague callers pass the connection context, matching C's path_x->cnx->cwin_blocked latch use.
picoquic/cc_common.c:picoquic_cc_slow_st.fix_summary: Changed slow_start_increase, slow_start_increase_ex, and slow_start_increase_ex2 to take Connection and gate growth on connection.cwin_blocked; updated BBR, BBR1, Cubic, and Prague callers to pass the connection context.
verification: cargo test compiled but did not complete as a pass gate: broad existing integration failures were printed and cnxstress tests exceeded 60s

picoquic/config.c:config_parse_target_ve.analysis: Rust now matches the C uint32_t digit loop, including wrapping overflow and zero on invalid hex characters.
picoquic/config.c:config_parse_target_ve.confirmation_analysis: Current Rust matches the C hex digit loop: ASCII hex digits accumulate into u32, invalid bytes return 0, empty or wrapped-to-zero inputs return 0, and overflow wraps modulo 2^32.
picoquic/config.c:config_parse_target_ve.fix_summary: Replaced u32::from_str_radix with byte-by-byte hex parsing using wrapping u32 accumulation; added focused tests for valid digits, invalid input, and overlong wraparound.

picoquic/config.c:config_set_option.analysis: Confirmed mismatch: ECH server handling accepted a single value and left ech_config_file unchanged, unlike C's second config_set_string_param call.
picoquic/config.c:config_set_option.confirmation_analysis: Current Rust EchServer handling now calls config_set_string_param for both parameter 0 and parameter 1. The one-value set_option path sets ech_key_file, clears ech_config_file, and returns InvalidArgument, matching the C helper-call sequence.
picoquic/config.c:config_set_option.fix_summary: Updated EchServer to use config_set_string_param semantics for key and config file, requiring parameter 1 and clearing ech_config_file on missing or empty parameter; added focused ECH option tests.

picoquic/config.c:picoquic_config_comman.analysis: Rust now preserves the C behavior for unrecognized extended option strings: report the unknown option but return success without consuming argv.
picoquic/config.c:picoquic_config_comman.confirmation_analysis: Current Rust matches C for unknown extended options: it reports to stderr, returns success, and leaves argv/p_optind/config untouched; long-name lookup also uses C-style table-order prefix matching.
picoquic/config.c:picoquic_config_comman.fix_summary: Updated command_line_ex to return Ok(()) on unknown options after stderr reporting; aligned long-name lookup with C-style prefix matching; added focused unit coverage.

picoquic/config.c:picoquic_config_get_co.analysis: Rust command-line parsing now matches C long-option prefix lookup semantics: abbreviated names such as --long resolve through the same table-order prefix helper used by command_line_ex, while overlong names remain unknown.
picoquic/config.c:picoquic_config_get_co.confirmation_analysis: Actual current Rust item delegates to parse_option_string; short options use table-order letter lookup and long options use table-order prefix lookup, matching the C helper semantics. The prompt body is the adjacent value helper span, not the current item.
picoquic/config.c:picoquic_config_get_co.fix_summary: Added focused unit coverage for C-style abbreviated long-option lookup through picoquic_config_get_command_line_option_index and Config::command_line_ex.

picoquic/config.c:picoquic_config_usage_.analysis: Confirmed Rust write_usage omitted the C CC_ALGO supported-values line; it now emits registered congestion-control algorithm IDs with the C indentation/comma/period formatting when the registry is non-empty.
picoquic/config.c:picoquic_config_usage_.confirmation_analysis: Rust write_usage now mirrors the C option-table output and CC_ALGO supported-values continuation line, including non-empty registry gating, 18-space indent, comma separators, and final period.
picoquic/config.c:picoquic_config_usage_.fix_summary: Aligned the CC_ALGO help text with C and added the registry-driven supported-values output in Config::write_usage.
verification: cargo test config_usage (failed: current Rust test registers all algorithms while the golden fixture expects only newreno, cubic, bbr; fixture also has an existing qlog help-text mismatch)

picoquic/config.c:picoquic_create_and_co.analysis: Confirmed repair needed. Rust now uses BBR fallback with the option string, applies preferred addresses to default transport parameters, and keeps the literal C ECH branch behavior.
picoquic/config.c:picoquic_create_and_co.confirmation_analysis: Current Rust now matches the relevant C behavior for BBR fallback with option string, preferred-address setup, and ECH branch/failure handling.
picoquic/config.c:picoquic_create_and_co.fix_summary: Changed congestion fallback to use the linked BBR algorithm directly instead of leaving any path that could retain Quic::new's NewReno default.

picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_apply_reset_s.analysis: Current Rust already preserves the C fall-through behavior: invalid local unidirectional RESET_STREAM records a connection error and sets the eventual return to None, but still runs stream lookup/create, final-offset validation, flow-control check, and reset handling.

picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_check_frame_n.analysis: Rust retransmission decision logic now mirrors the C stateful cases instead of only handling a shallow subset.
picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_check_frame_n.confirmation_analysis: Top-level Rust now covers the previously missing frame classes, but PATH_RESPONSE repeat classification still differs from C.
picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_check_frame_n.confirmation_fix_summary: C picoquic_should_repeat_path_response_frame only checks each path's first_tuple, while Rust should_repeat_path_response_frame searches all tuples; a PATH_RESPONSE tied to a non-first tuple can produce a different no_need_to_repeat result.
picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_check_frame_n.fix_summary: Expanded check_frame_needs_repeat with stream SACK/reset handling, flow-control and blocked-frame checks, datagram/token/crypto/CID/reset/stop decisions, ack-frequency and multipath path-frame repeat handling, and preserved C-style output flag semantics.

picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_compute_ack_g.analysis: Rust now follows the translated helper sequence and includes the C conservative high-smoothed-RTT correction and final 32-packet cap.
picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_compute_ack_g.confirmation_analysis: Rust now mirrors the C helper sequence, high-smoothed-RTT conservative correction, ACK transmission-time cap, RTT-target gap correction, and final 32-packet cap. Safe saturation/division guards do not indicate a real translation mismatch for valid state.
picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_compute_ack_g.fix_summary: Reworked compute_ack_gap_and_delay to call packet-window, ACK-delay, and ACK-gap helpers, then added return-rate ACK transmission correction, RTT-target gap correction, and final cap.

picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_copy_stream_f.analysis: Rust now represents C's nullable connection path; no-connection retransmit copying skips stream lookup instead of suppressing missing-stream data.
picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_copy_stream_f.confirmation_analysis: Rust now represents the nullable C connection path: None maps to NoConnection, which skips stream lookup and keeps the frame needed, while production callers still pass a real Connection and preserve missing/reset/acked suppression.
picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_copy_stream_f.fix_summary: Added StreamFrameRetransmitContext with Connection and NoConnection modes, kept production caller using a real connection, and added owned-file unit coverage for pure no-connection copy behavior.

picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_copy_stream_f.analysis: Current Rust implementation already matches the C wrapper behavior: priority queue loop, single-frame retransmit delegation, dequeue/requeue handling, more_data propagation, and corrupted-frame fallback are present.
picoquic/frames.c:picoquic_copy_stream_f.confirmation_analysis: Current Rust wrapper matches the C control flow: it walks the priority-ordered repeat queue, stops above current_priority with more_data set, delegates to the single-frame retransmit helper, repeats only after dequeue while space remains, handles dequeue/requeue through the helper, and resets to the original buffer position with an internal error on corrupted-frame failure.

picoquic/logwriter.c:binlog_close_connec.analysis: Rust close path now includes the C-observable autoqlog callback and open-log accounting after closing an active binlog handle.
picoquic/logwriter.c:binlog_close_connec.confirmation_analysis: Rust close_connection now matches the C close-side effects for an active binlog handle: close record, flush, close/drop handle, conditional autoqlog callback before clearing the binlog file name, and guarded open-log decrement.
picoquic/logwriter.c:binlog_close_connec.fix_summary: Closed/flushed the binlog handle before autoqlog, ran autoqlog when qlog_dir and autoqlog_fn are set, cleared binlog_file_name, and decremented current_number_of_open_logs when positive.

picoquic/logwriter.c:binlog_new_connecti.analysis: Rust now matches the C behavior: binlog new_connection opens and names the per-connection file, enforces the open-log cap, updates bookkeeping, and writes the start event through installed binlog dispatch.
picoquic/logwriter.c:binlog_new_connecti.confirmation_analysis: Rust now opens and names the per-connection binlog, enforces the open-log cap, updates bookkeeping, writes the new-connection event, and binlog enablement installs the dispatch backend.
picoquic/logwriter.c:binlog_new_connecti.fix_summary: Implemented binlog file creation/bookkeeping in Connection::new_connection and wired Quic::enable_binlog to install the binlog Logger backend.

picoquic/logwriter.c:binlog_outgoing_pac.analysis: Confirmed outgoing binlog parsing now matches the C path for nonzero short-header remote CID offsets and version-specific long-header packet type decoding.
picoquic/logwriter.c:binlog_outgoing_pac.confirmation_analysis: Rust outgoing_packet now mirrors the C outgoing parse path: short headers use the connection path-0 remote CID length, long headers use supported-version packet-type decoding, and the PN/checksum adjustments match before packet logging.
picoquic/logwriter.c:binlog_outgoing_pac.fix_summary: Added focused regression tests for outgoing short headers with a connection remote CID and QUIC v2 long-header type parsing in rs/fq/src/binlog.rs.

picoquic/logwriter.c:picoquic_enable_bin.analysis: Current Rust source already installs a real BinlogLogger in Quic.bin_log_fns and propagates it to existing connections; new connections also clone the context logger, matching the C vtable enable behavior.
picoquic/logwriter.c:picoquic_enable_bin.confirmation_analysis: Rust now installs a real BinlogLogger in Quic.bin_log_fns, propagates it to existing connections, and new connections clone the context logger; BinlogLogger dispatches new_connection to the binlog implementation, matching the C vtable enable behavior in this Rust architecture.

picoquic/logwriter.c:picoquic_log_stream.analysis: Confirmed mismatch: length-bearing STREAM logging used the pre-length header length, omitting or undercounting the encoded length varint. Rust now logs through the parsed length varint plus the payload preview and preserves C-style short-frame error logging.
picoquic/logwriter.c:picoquic_log_stream.confirmation_analysis: Rust now computes the logged header length after read_length, so length-bearing STREAM frames include the encoded length varint plus the payload preview; zero-length and short parse-error logging are acceptable.
picoquic/logwriter.c:picoquic_log_stream.fix_summary: Updated log_stream_frame header-length accounting after read_length, added cautious STREAM parse-error logging, and added focused unit tests for length-bearing, zero-length, and short STREAM frames.
